container_info.description:
**Product Overview**

Mobile Service Hub is a web-based service booking and management system designed to address the challenges customers face in finding reliable mobile repair services, comparing prices, and booking technicians. The platform also supports service centers in managing service requests, technicians, and billing. The system targets Super Admins, Service Center Admins, Technicians, and Customers, providing a centralized solution for booking and managing mobile repair services.

**Main Objectives**
- Centralize mobile repair service bookings for customers
- Enable efficient management of jobs, technicians, and billing for service centers
- Support multiple user roles: Super Admin, Service Center Admin, Technician, Customer

**Expected Outcomes**
- Streamlined booking process for customers
- Improved operational efficiency for service centers
- Transparent billing and reporting
- Scalable platform for future enhancements (e.g., online payments, inventory management, customer feedback)
container_info.reasoning: The application is explicitly described as a web-based service booking and management system and the container is labeled 'frontend'. The Dockerfile summary includes front-end toolchains and CLIs such as nodejs, npm, yarn, typescript, create-react-app, @vue/cli, and @angular/cli. For a multi-role, SPA-like management and booking UI React is a strong fit and create-react-app is present in the image, making React the most suitable choice for the frontend monolith.
requirements: nodejs (runtime) and npm or yarn - already present in container
create-react-app (or minimal react + vite) for project scaffolding (use create-react-app CLI if present)

a lightweight dev server (react-scripts start or vite) for headless operation
build tool: npm run build (react-scripts build) or vite build
minimal test dependency (jest or react-scripts test) for basic validation, optional and lightweight
HEADLESS environment variables: NODE_ENV=development, PORT (optional) configured

steps.name: Environment setup and persistence
steps.description: Create workspace, verify node and npm presence and versions (Node >=16), and write a safe /etc/profile.d/react_dev_env.sh that exports NODE_ENV, HOST and conditionally appends npm global bin if present. Do not rely on this file for immediate non-interactive execution; scripts explicitly export environment variables when run. Idempotent and non-destructive.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/mobile-service-hub-41952-42033/MobileServiceHubMonolith"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node not found; ensure nodejs is installed" >&2; exit 2; }
NODE_V_RAW=$(node -v 2>/dev/null || true)
NODE_MAJOR=$(printf "%s" "$NODE_V_RAW" | sed -n 's/^v\?\([0-9]\+\).*/\1/p' || true)
if [ -z "$NODE_MAJOR" ] || ! printf "%s" "$NODE_MAJOR" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' || [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 16 ]; then
  echo "Node >=16 required for CRA v5+. Found: ${NODE_V_RAW:-unknown}." >&2
  exit 3
fi
command -v npm >/dev/null || { echo "npm not found; ensure npm is available" >&2; exit 4; }
# best-effort npm global bin
NPM_G_BIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || printf "%s" "${HOME}/.npm-global/bin")
PROFILE_FILE=/etc/profile.d/react_dev_env.sh
# write safe, minimal profile (use sudo). Conditional PATH append checks directory existence at runtime.
sudo bash -c "cat > '$PROFILE_FILE' <<'EOF'
# MobileServiceHubMonolith development env (auto-generated)
export NODE_ENV=development
export HOST=0.0.0.0
# PORT can be set per-session: export PORT=3000
# Conditionally add npm global bin if it exists when a shell starts
if [ -n \"${NPM_G_BIN}\" ] && [ -d \"${NPM_G_BIN}\" ] && ! echo \"\$PATH\" | /bin/grep -q -- \"${NPM_G_BIN}\"; then
  export PATH=\"${NPM_G_BIN}:\$PATH\"
fi
EOF"
sudo chmod 0644 "$PROFILE_FILE"
node -v || true
npm -v || true
exit 0

steps.name: Detect & fix malformed /etc/profile.d entries
steps.description: Detect if /etc/profile.d/react_dev_env.sh or other files in /etc/profile.d inject syntax errors or reference non-existent dirs. If a malformed react_dev_env.sh is found, rename it to .broken and write a corrected safe version. This prevents non-interactive shells from failing. Requires sudo.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PROFILE=/etc/profile.d/react_dev_env.sh
if [ -f "$PROFILE" ]; then
  # quick syntax check by sourcing in a subshell; capture errors
  if ! sudo bash -n "$PROFILE" 2>/tmp/react_profile_check.err; then
    sudo mv "$PROFILE" "$PROFILE.broken" || true
    # write a safe replacement
    NPM_G_BIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || printf "%s" "${HOME}/.npm-global/bin")
    sudo bash -c "cat > '$PROFILE' <<'EOF'
# Fixed MobileServiceHubMonolith development env (auto-generated)
export NODE_ENV=development
export HOST=0.0.0.0
# PORT may be set per-session
if [ -n \"${NPM_G_BIN}\" ] && [ -d \"${NPM_G_BIN}\" ] && ! echo \"\$PATH\" | /bin/grep -q -- \"${NPM_G_BIN}\"; then
  export PATH=\"${NPM_G_BIN}:\$PATH\"
fi
EOF"
    sudo chmod 0644 "$PROFILE"
  fi
fi
exit 0

steps.name: Ensure workspace permissions for agent
steps.description: Ensure the agent user can create, chmod and execute helper scripts in the workspace and .init directory. If ownership or permissions prevent creating executables, fix them (chown/chmod). Uses sudo only when necessary and is idempotent.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/mobile-service-hub-41952-33/MobileServiceHubMonolith"
# Use authoritative workspace from container info
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/mobile-service-hub-41952-42033/MobileServiceHubMonolith"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" "$WORKSPACE/.init"
# If current user can't create executables, fix ownership to current user
TEST_FILE="$WORKSPACE/.init/.perm_test"
touch "$TEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! chmod +x "$TEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
  # attempt to chown workspace to current user
  sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$WORKSPACE" || true
  sudo chmod -R u+rwX "$WORKSPACE" || true
  touch "$TEST_FILE" || true
  chmod +x "$TEST_FILE" || true
fi
rm -f "$TEST_FILE" || true
exit 0

steps.name: Install dependencies
steps.description: Install project dependencies in workspace. Prefer yarn if yarn.lock exists and yarn is present; otherwise use npm. Detect TypeScript via package.json or tsconfig.json and install types using the same package manager. Non-interactive, fail-fast, validate node_modules creation and write .local_bin_path for downstream steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export NODE_ENV=development HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=${PORT:-3000}
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/mobile-service-hub-41952-42033/MobileServiceHubMonolith"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
USE_YARN=0
if [ -f yarn.lock ] && command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1; then USE_YARN=1; fi
if [ "$USE_YARN" -eq 1 ]; then
  yarn install --network-timeout 600000 --frozen-lockfile || { echo "yarn install failed" >&2; exit 9; }
else
  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
    npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --prefer-offline --no-progress || npm i --no-audit --no-fund --no-progress || { echo "npm install failed" >&2; exit 10; }
  else
    npm i --no-audit --no-fund --no-progress || { echo "npm install failed" >&2; exit 10; }
  fi
fi
# detect TS
HAS_TS=0
if node -e "try{const fs=require('fs'); const pj=require('./package.json'); if ((pj.devDependencies&&pj.devDependencies.typescript) || (pj.dependencies&&pj.dependencies.typescript)) process.exit(0); if (fs.existsSync('tsconfig.json')) process.exit(0); process.exit(1);}catch(e){process.exit(1)}" 2>/dev/null; then HAS_TS=1; fi
if [ "$HAS_TS" -eq 1 ]; then
  if [ "$USE_YARN" -eq 1 ]; then yarn add --dev typescript @types/react @types/react-dom || { echo "yarn add types failed" >&2; exit 11; } else npm i --save-dev typescript @types/react @types/react-dom --no-audit --no-fund --no-progress || { echo "npm add types failed" >&2; exit 12; }; fi
fi
[ -d node_modules ] || { echo "node_modules missing after install" >&2; exit 13; }
printf "%s" "$WORKSPACE/node_modules/.bin" > .local_bin_path || true
node -v || true
if [ "$USE_YARN" -eq 1 ]; then yarn -v || true; else npm -v || true; fi
exit 0

  if [ "$USE_YARN" -eq 1 ]; then yarn test --watchAll=false || { echo "yarn test failed" >&2; exit 15; } else npm test -- --watchAll=false || { echo "npm test failed" >&2; exit 16; } fi

steps.name: Start dev server (background)
steps.description: Start the project's dev server in background using local binaries when available. Use setsid + exec so background leader PID maps to server process. Persist logs to /tmp/react_dev.log and leader PID to /tmp/react_dev.pid. Export NODE_ENV/HOST/PORT explicitly. This step depends on permission and profile remediation steps so non-interactive shells are not broken and scripts can be chmod'd.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export NODE_ENV=development HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=${PORT:-3000}
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/mobile-service-hub-41952-42033/MobileServiceHubMonolith"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
LOG=/tmp/react_dev.log
PID_FILE=/tmp/react_dev.pid
USE_YARN=0
if [ -f yarn.lock ] && command -v yarn >/dev/null 2>&1; then USE_YARN=1; fi
LOCAL_START="./node_modules/.bin/react-scripts"
if [ -x "$LOCAL_START" ]; then
  setsid sh -c "exec \"$LOCAL_START\" start" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
else
  if [ "$USE_YARN" -eq 1 ]; then
    setsid sh -c "exec yarn start" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
  else
    setsid sh -c "exec npm start" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
  fi
fi
LEADER_PID=$!
printf "%s" "$LEADER_PID" > "$PID_FILE"
sleep 1
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$LEADER_PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
printf "leader=%s pgid=%s log=%s\n" "$LEADER_PID" "$PGID" "$LOG"
exit 0
